findings.description: SINGLE-CALL ATOMICITY vs 500-ROW CHUNKING. Spec: "rewrite each view tab as a SINGLE batchUpdate ... leaving no half-written window." Code: runtime/src/adapters.rs:210 `write_data_rows` splits the grid with `grid.chunks(VIEW_WRITE_CHUNK_ROWS)` where `pub const VIEW_WRITE_CHUNK_ROWS: usize = 500` (line 225), issuing one separate `self.api.update_range('{name}'!A{2 + i*500}:Z, chunk)` per chunk. tests/adapters.rs:`view_republish_writes_large_tabs_in_row_chunks` pins `update_count == 1` at exactly 500 rows and `update_count == 2` at 501 — i.e. a >500-row tab is provably NOT one call. If chunk 2 fails after chunk 1 lands, the result is exactly the half-written window the spec forbids, and the trait doc's promise (`Err(PublishFailed)` ... "leaving the tab as-is") plus the test `failed_republish_marks_stale_writes_banner_and_retries` ("failed publish lands nothing") hold only because the fake fails atomically. Both directions hit this independently: all 3 A-runs built exactly one API round-trip per tab with update+truncate as ordered Requests; all 3 B-runs reconstructed the 500 constant, the `2 + i*500` anchor, and the 500/501 boundary — none of which the spec text contains.

TRUNCATION IS NEVER ISSUED IN THE PRODUCTION PATH. Spec: "truncates the residual tail to the exact row count ... no leftover stale rows." All 3 A-runs emit an explicit tail-removal request (`deleteDimension` over rows [new_len, current_row_count)) sized from a read row count. The real `ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view` emits NO clear, delete, or truncate operation of any kind — only `update_range` calls whose ranges are `'{name}'!A{start}:Z`. The `SheetsApi` primitive does expose a clear (module doc line 11: "the one primitive's read/append/update/clear") and it is never called. Truncation is therefore a property of the fakes, not of the system: `InMemorySheetsView::batch_update_view` does `existing.rows = tab.rows.clone()` (testkit.rs:178, wholesale replace), and the adapter doc (adapters.rs:173) says the write is "one `update_range`, which the FakeSheetsApi tail-truncates." The spec's central obligation is pinned only by fake semantics; `sheets-view/tests/republish.rs::republish_is_atomic_batchupdate_with_tail_truncate` (3 rows → 1 row) exercises the fake's `Vec` replacement, not any truncation request.

FROZEN HEADER AND DATA_START_ROW = 2 — the rewrite is scoped to rows 2..N and row 1 is immutable, none of which the spec states. Spec says "rewrite each view tab" and "the exact row count" with no notion of a header. Code: `pub const DATA_START_ROW: u32 = 2` (lib.rs:148); every range is anchored at row 2 (`'{name}'!A2:Z`); the header is written exactly once, only on the missing-tab bootstrap (`update_range('{tab}'!A1, [tab.header])`, adapters.rs:254); and the testkit enforces byte-identical headers on republish with an UNCONDITIONAL `assert_eq!(existing.header, tab.header, "the frozen header must never be rewritten on republish")` (testkit.rs:174) — a panic in release builds, not a debug_assert. Test `view_republish_and_marks_read_back_ride_the_one_primitive` asserts `grid[0][0] == "Symbol"` survives and `DATA_START_ROW == 2`. All 3 B-runs reconstructed this as a first-class requirement; zero A-runs invented a frozen header (all three wrote from row 0 / index 0 including the header in the rewritten window).

MISSING-TAB BOOTSTRAP (write-implies-create) is a whole code path the spec never mentions. adapters.rs:249-258: when the data write returns `is_missing_tab(e)`, the adapter calls `ensure_sheet(&tab.name)`, writes the segment-owned header to `'{tab}'!A1`, then RETRIES the data write — each step mapping failure to `ViewError::PublishFailed`. The spec text presumes the tab exists and says nothing about creation, header bootstrap, or a retry. All 3 B-runs recovered this (B1 SHEET-PUB-005, B2 R6, B3 PUB-013); no A-run considered it.

FAILURE SEMANTICS BEYOND THE SPEC: stale flags + in-tab STALE banner. Spec says only what a successful rewrite must look like. Code (lib.rs:974-988): on `batch_update_view` error the `Publisher` sets `all_ok = false`, inserts the tab into a persistent `stale` set, and writes a best-effort banner `format!("STALE — last sync {stale_banner_quote_ts}")`; the banner write's own failure is swallowed (`let _ = ...`) while the stale flag persists; a later success `self.stale.remove(&tab.name)` clears it. The banner lands at the hard-coded cell `'{tab}'!AA1` (adapters.rs:309). Tests `failed_republish_marks_stale_writes_banner_and_retries` and `banner_write_failure_leaves_tui_as_staleness_surface` pin all of it. All 3 B-runs reconstructed the banner text and the swallow-the-banner-failure rule; B3 even recovered the `AA1` anchor.

ADVISORY WRITE-LOCK PRECONDITION. The spec's "no half-written window" is silent on concurrency, yet the code's actual protection against a concurrent mutator is a lock: `Publisher::republish` calls `lock.acquire()` BEFORE any tab is touched and on `Err` returns `RepublishOutcome { published: false, stale_tabs: <unchanged> }` writing nothing (lib.rs:964-972). Test `republish_under_a_held_lock_writes_nothing` asserts nothing lands; `republish_acquires_the_lock_before_mutating` asserts `acquire_count() == 1` (one acquisition for the whole multi-tab republish, not per tab). All 3 B-runs surfaced the held-lock refusal and the `published: false` outcome; no A-run has any locking concept.

HARD 26-COLUMN WINDOW AND NO COLUMN TRUNCATION. Every range the adapter builds is `'{tab}'!A{row}:Z` (adapters.rs:200, 216, 279) — an undeclared cap of columns A..Z and a fixed right edge the spec's "the new range" never bounds. Residual COLUMNS are never truncated (only the `:Z` edge exists). Notably A2 independently invented column-tail truncation (`DeleteDimension` on Columns when `current_cols > width`) from the same spec text and the code has no such behavior, so the spec under-determines the column axis in both directions. B3 pinned the `'<tab>'!A2:Z` range form explicitly.

EMPTY-VIEW CASE: "exact row count" includes zero, and the code cannot reach it. All 3 A-runs handled an empty grid explicitly (emit truncation only, clamped to a 1-row floor for the Sheets zero-row rule). Code: `write_data_rows` short-circuits an empty grid to `self.api.update_range(&Self::data_range(name), grid)` with an EMPTY payload (adapters.rs:211-213). An empty values update carries no cells and — with no accompanying clear — cannot remove the prior body, so a view that drops from N rows to 0 (all positions sold) leaves every prior row stale. The in-memory fake hides this: it replaces `rows` with an empty `Vec`. No test covers the N→0 transition (the closest, `republish_is_atomic_batchupdate_with_tail_truncate`, goes 3→1).

REPUBLISH OUTCOME IS COUPLED TO A TAB-ORDER REASSERT THE SPEC NEVER MENTIONS. After all tabs are rewritten, `Publisher::republish` calls `set_tab_order(&workbook_tab_order())` over a 10-entry ordering (Positions, Open Lots, Realized, Tax, History, Tax Rules, Residency, Platforms & Aliases, Ledger Events, Tax Events) and, on failure, sets `published: false` WITHOUT flagging any tab stale (lib.rs:991-994) — so a successful rewrite of every tab can still report not-published. The spec scopes the requirement to per-tab rewrite+truncate only. B3 recovered this exactly (PUB-014 / PUB-023); B1 and B2 omitted it — the one point of genuine B-side divergence.

CELL-TYPING CONTRACT CARRIED INSIDE THE REWRITE OBLIGATION. The `SheetsViewClient::batch_update_view` doc (lib.rs:439-448) makes value/formula typing part of the same contract the spec sentence covers: a `Cell::Value` must be written as `userEnteredValue`, NOT a forced `stringValue`, so `"20.0000%"` (produced by `fmt_ppm`) coerces to the numeric fraction 0.20 that the live `=G*H` / `=G*(1-H)` post-tax formulas multiply; a `Cell::Formula` is written as a formula including its leading `=`. The adapter flattens both to `c.text()` (adapters.rs:241) and pushes raw strings through the primitive, so the typing guarantee is unenforced at the seam and untested. The spec text says nothing about cell typing; all 3 B-runs nonetheless reconstructed the percent→0.20 coercion rule verbatim.

UNDER-SPECIFIED MECHANISM — the spec leaves the how of "single batchUpdate" open enough that the three A-runs diverged and the code took a fourth route. Unresolved by the text: (a) whether truncation removes rows or blanks cells — all 3 A-runs chose `deleteDimension`, the code does neither; (b) whether the grid must be grown before the write — A1 and A2 emit `appendDimension` first, A3 relies on `updateCells` auto-expanding and flags the risk; (c) the Sheets zero-row-grid rule, which all 3 A-runs patched with an invented `keep = max(new_len, 1)` floor; (d) whether "single batchUpdate" is per-tab or workbook-wide (A3 argued the point explicitly from "each"); (e) how a tab is addressed (numeric `sheetId` in all A-runs vs quoted A1 string ranges `'{tab}'!A2:Z` in the code). The spec cannot adjudicate any of these against the implementation.

notes: Classified BD-DRIFT: the chunking/atomicity divergence is surfaced from both sides of the round trip — A-side because the spec's \"single batchUpdate\" and \"no half-written window\" force a one-call design the code does not implement, B-side because the code pins a VIEW_WRITE_CHUNK_ROWS = 500 multi-call boundary (with a dedicated test at 500/501) that the spec never states. A second, arguably equally severe A-only finding sits underneath: the spec's headline obligation — truncate the residual tail — has NO production implementation at all. ViewSheetsAdapter issues only update_range calls; there is no clear/delete anywhere, even though the SheetsApi primitive exposes a clear per the module doc. Every truncation assertion in the suite runs against a fake that replaces a Rust Vec (InMemorySheetsView) or truncates by fiat (FakeSheetsApi), so a real Sheets values.update would leave the stale tail the spec forbids. Note also that the word \"batchUpdate\" survives only in the trait name and doc comments (`batch_update_view`, \"Atomically rewrite a view tab as a single batchUpdate\") — the implementation is a values-style range update. A-side stability: all 3 runs agreed on the load-bearing reading (one HTTP call per tab containing update + deleteDimension, all-or-nothing failure, keep>=1 row floor); they split only on growth handling (A1/A2 appendDimension vs A3 implicit expansion) and column-tail truncation (A2 only) — variation in invented sub-decisions, not in interpretation. B-side stability: all 3 runs independently named DATA_START_ROW = 2, the never-rewritten frozen header with its unconditional assertion, wholesale-replace-plus-truncate with the 3-rows-then-1-row example, VIEW_WRITE_CHUNK_ROWS = 500 with the 500/501 boundary, the empty-set write of 'tab'!A2:Z, the missing-tab bootstrap, PublishFailed + stale flag + best-effort STALE banner with swallowed banner failure, and the held-lock published:false refusal. The only divergence is additive: B3 alone recovered the tab-order reassert and the AA1 banner anchor. Findings 3-7 and 9-10 are all pure code-side surplus measured against a one-sentence spec that mentions none of it — the spec sentence describes roughly the narrowest slice of what batch_update_view actually guarantees.
